title: Restore the Windows arm64 check on R-release
description:
Adds `windows-11-arm` back to CI now that adbcdrivermanager compiles with aarch64 RTools and binaries are available on r-universe.

This uses the devel version of pak because the released version of pak doesn't yet support finding binaries for windows-11-arm and arrow isn't currently compiling cleanly with pak on windows-11-arm. I added a TODO to remove the workaround once a new version of pak is released.

This was previously removed in #71. The fix (apache/arrow-adbc#4591) shipped in ADBC 25 (2026-10-21), and adbcdrivermanager 0.25.0 has been on CRAN since 2026-10-27.

title: Treat empty ADBC parameter names as positional
description:
Unnamed ADBC parameter fields are empty strings, but `dbBind()` classifies them as named placeholders and rejects positional values. Require nonempty field names in the named-schema check so valid positional parameters bind without changing driver metadata.

The regression uses unnamed metadata with SQLite and covers NULLs, rebinding, wrong parameter counts and rejection of named input for positional placeholders.

Fixes #127.

Validation: `testthat::test_local(filter="parameters")`: 78 assertions passed, zero failures, warnings or skips. The native Redis integration also passed single/multiple positional parameters, NULLs and rebinding against an isolated patched adbi install.

Assisted by OpenAI Codex.

title: Raise an error, not a warning, in the strict `bigint` modes
description:
## Summary

- In the strict `bigint` modes, `"integer-strict"` (the default) and `"numeric-strict"`, the conversion handler passed nanoarrow's lossy-conversion warning to `stop()`, which signals a condition object unchanged. The failure therefore stayed a warning: neither `tryCatch(error = )` nor `try()` caught it, so the script halted, and a handler that muffles warnings, as `suppressWarnings()` and testthat do, resumed the conversion through the restart of nanoarrow's `warning()` call, which returned `NA` or a rounded value.
- The handler now raises the warning's message, unchanged, as an error. A 64-bit value that a strict mode cannot represent fails as the `bigint` documentation describes, whatever handlers are in place.
- The new test in `test-fetch.R` covers both strict modes under `suppressWarnings()` and fails on `main`.
- None of the reverse dependencies relies on the old warning: db2pq reads adbi results through the Arrow path, which does not convert 64-bit values, fabricQueryR connects with `bigint = "integer64"`, and the adbc test of dbplyr fetches small integers only.

Fixes #111

title: Consume a pending deferred close when the connection is released
description:
## Summary

- Unset the flag that marks a deferred close where `dbDisconnect()` releases the connection, as proposed in #123. Nothing unset it once the deferred close had run, so clearing a result a second time ran `dbDisconnect()` again, which warned that the connection and the database were already released, next to the warning about the statement that the DBI specification asks for. A forced close after a deferred one left the flag set as well, so clearing one of the results it cleared warned the same way.
- Unsetting the flag in `rm_result()` instead, ahead of the deferred close, would miss the forced close, because `clear_results()` restores the flag on exit (#124) before the forced close releases the connection.
- Only warnings change, so there is no NEWS entry, as for #124. None of the three CRAN reverse dependencies (db2pq, dbplyr and fabricQueryR, all through Suggests) refers to these warnings.
- Two new tests in `test-clear-result.R` cover the two cases, and both fail on `main`. Each nests an `expect_no_warning()` for the connection and database warnings inside the `expect_warning()` for the statement's, since under testthat's 2nd edition `expect_warning()` alone would swallow them.

Fixes #123

title: Hold off a deferred close while adbi clears results itself
description:
## Summary

- Hold off a pending deferred close in `clear_results()` while it clears, with the flag saved, unset and restored on exit, as proposed in #120. Clearing the last result there ran the deferred close inside a forced `dbDisconnect()`, which then warned that the connection and the database were already released, and inside the next query sent under `options(adbi.allow_multiple_results = FALSE)`, where the new statement was still open and both releases failed with a message each. Since #121, the forced case hits with any number of open results, not only with one.
- The connection ended up in the right state either way, closed by the forced close or once the new result was cleared, so only the warnings and messages change, and there is no NEWS entry. None of the three CRAN reverse dependencies (db2pq, dbplyr and fabricQueryR, all through Suggests) refers to these warnings or to either option.
- Two new tests in `test-clear-result.R` cover the two cases, and both fail on `main`. They assert the absence of the stray conditions with `expect_no_warning()` and `expect_no_message()`, because under testthat's 2nd edition, which adbi runs, `expect_warning()` swallows any further warnings.
- Clearing a result a second time after a deferred close still runs the close again. That is a separate trigger with its own fix in `dbDisconnect()`, filed as #123.

Fixes #120

title: Pin blockr.ci to v0.1.1 and let Dependabot propose upgrades
description:
## Summary

- Pins the `release` job to blockr.ci's v0.1.1 tag. The blockr.ci releases are immutable, so the tag cannot be moved to another commit. The issue named v0.1.0, but v0.1.1 was published after it was filed and is the commit `@main` resolves to today, so the gate runs the same code as before.
- Adds `.github/dependabot.yml` for the `github-actions` ecosystem, checked weekly, as blockr.ci's README suggests. It covers every action in `rcc.yaml`, so their upgrades arrive as pull requests too.
- Nothing needs adding to Dependabot secrets, since the `release` call passes none: blockr.ci's `BLOCKR_PAT` falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- A Dependabot pull request that bumps the pin runs the gate only once labelled `release`, and the comment on the job now says so.

Fixes #117

title: Remove a cleared result by identity, not by its position
description:
## Summary

- Keep a connection's open results in a hash table from `utils::hashtab("address")`, keyed by each result's metadata environment, which every copy of a result shares. Clearing a result removes its entry by that identity rather than whatever sat at the position recorded when it was sent, in constant time: clearing 3,000 open results takes 0.4 s against 0.9 s on `main`. Removing an entry that is already gone does nothing.
- This raises the R floor to 4.2.0, where `hashtab()` arrived, moves the CI job for the oldest R from 4.1 to 4.2, and moves `utils` from Suggests to Imports. The help page of `hashtab()` marks it as experimental. Earlier commits here matched entries by identity in R, which took 16 s for 3,000, and then by generated ids, which needed a counter with a limit.
- The position went stale once a result sent earlier was cleared. The NEWS entry names the condition as clearing a result while one sent after it is still open; in a simulation of every send and clear order of up to six results under the old scheme, each order with such a clear ended with a result still registered, and every other order with none.
- New tests in `test-clear-result.R` clear results oldest first ahead of each disconnect that reads the registry: a plain one, a forced one, and the deferred one that clearing the last result runs. All three fail on `main`.
- A forced `dbDisconnect()` after a deferred one now warns that the connection and the database are already released with several results open too, as it already did on `main` with one. The deferred close fires inside the forced one, and with several results `main` escaped it only because the registry never emptied. Filed as #120, with a fix.

Fixes #119

title: Document the `bigint` values and the `integer-strict` default
description:
## Summary

- The `bigint` argument of `dbConnect()` is now documented with the default it has had since 641ec8b, `"integer-strict"`, rather than `bit64::integer64` or `character`.
- Its documentation lists all six accepted values and says what the two strict modes do, which no help page did before.
- The `bigint` argument of `dbSendQuery()` links to that list. Its example now overrides the default with `"numeric"`, as the `"integer"` it used stopped changing the result once `"integer-strict"` became the default.

Fixes #112

title: Clear the result when a sent query fails to bind or run
description:
## Summary

- Both `dbSendQuery()` and `dbSendQueryArrow()` register their result with the connection before binding `params` or running the query. When either step fails, the method errors without returning the result, so the caller has nothing to clear and `dbDisconnect()` only marks the connection for release.
- Both methods now clear the result when binding or execution fails, with the same `on.exit()` guard that #114 added to `dbSendStatement()`. The error each call raises is unchanged, and DBI's `dbGetQuery()` and `dbGetQueryArrow()` methods go through these two, so they are covered as well.
- The new test sends a failing bind and a failing execution through each method on one connection, then expects `dbDisconnect()` to return `TRUE`. Without the fix it returns `FALSE`, with four results still registered.

Fixes #115

title: Run statements in `dbSendStatement()` and `dbBind()`
description:
## Summary

- Runs a statement from `dbSendStatement()` before the call returns when the resolved `immediate` is `TRUE`, and a bound statement in `dbBind()`, as DBI and DBItest specify. Unless sent with `immediate = TRUE`, statements used to run only once `dbGetRowsAffected()` asked for their count, so one cleared without that call never ran. With drivers that report parameter metadata, the default `immediate = NULL` resolves to `TRUE` for every statement without placeholders.
- Clears the result when a statement fails inside `dbSendStatement()`. Without this, moving execution there would undo part of #106: a failing `dbExecute()` would fail before it holds the result it clears on exit, and `dbDisconnect()` would then leave the connection open. The guard also covers a failing statement sent with `immediate = TRUE` or `params`, which already leaks its result on `main`. The query methods, `dbSendQuery()` and `dbSendQueryArrow()`, leak the same way and are left alone here.
- Changes the four expectations in `test-parameters.R` that `dbHasCompleted()` is `FALSE` right after a statement is bound, since the statement has run by then. The new tests in `test-send-statement.R` fail on `main` and pass with adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2 as with 0.11.0.1, the floor in Suggests. Through adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1 against PostgreSQL 17.11, statements likewise run when sent or bound, and failing ones leave the connection closable.
- With drivers that cannot report parameter metadata, such as Snowflake's, adbi cannot tell whether a statement has placeholders, so one sent with `immediate = NULL` and no `params` still runs only when bound or when `dbGetRowsAffected()` is called. The documentation now says so and points to `immediate = TRUE`.
- None of the CRAN reverse dependencies is affected: db2pq only sends queries, while dbplyr and fabricQueryR reach statements only through `dbExecute()`, which returns the same count and fails in the same call as before.

Fixes #113

title: Run statements without a result stream to count rows affected
description:
## Summary

- Runs `dbSendStatement()` results without a result stream, so that drivers built on ADBC's driver framework execute them as updates, as #92 traces. With adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, `dbExecute()`, `dbGetRowsAffected()` and `dbAppendTable()` now return the number of rows changed instead of `-1`. Through adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1 against PostgreSQL 17.11, statements with bound parameters reported `-1` as well and now get their count, while the counts it reported before are unchanged. Through DuckDB 1.5.5, every count stays as it was. None of the CRAN reverse dependencies relies on the `-1`: dbplyr discards the count, db2pq calls none of these functions, and fabricQueryR only passes it on in its write result.
- Drops the `rows_affected_callback` from the DBItest helper. It turned `-1` into a skip, which on `main` with DBItest 1.8.3 ended 200 of the 623 tests, any that ran a statement, including through `dbCreateTable()`, `dbRemoveTable()` or `dbAppendTable()`. Of those, 163 now pass. The other 37 fail for causes outside this change and join the skip list under them: 24 read an empty or all-`NULL` column back as integer, as adbcsqlite infers types from values (apache/arrow-adbc#1591); 10 are Arrow round trips that read `int64` back as double whatever the `bigint` (r-dbi/DBItest#334), which is also why `arrow_read_table_arrow` was already skipped; 2 lose 64-bit values outside the integer range under the default `bigint`, like the `data_64_bit_*` tests already skipped (r-dbi/DBItest#311, r-dbi/DBItest#334); and `append_roundtrip_raw` fails in `dbDataType()` on a list of raw vectors with a `NULL` entry (#108).
- Removes the skip-list entries for `begin_write_commit`, as #96 anticipated, and `arrow_write_table_arrow_visible_in_other_connection`, which were there only because of the callback; all their stages pass. Run without the skip list, the other entries that apply here still fail, apart from `begin_write_disconnect`, which never went through the callback and has #110. The entries adbi can drop now link the issues filed for them, #107 to #110, and the two listed as not reproducible in isolation link apache/arrow-adbc#4828: the failed append in `write_table_append_incompatible` leaves the connection in a transaction.
- Adds tests for the counts of unbound, bound and rebound statements and of `dbAppendTable()`, which fail on `main` and pass with adbcsqlite 0.11.0.1, the floor in Suggests, as with 0.24.0-2. They bind one row at a time, since the driver sums the counts of a multi-row binding only from 0.15.0 on and reported the last row's before. DBItest's `bind_multi_row_statement` covers the sum against the current release.
- Dropping the stream changes three other things. With adbcsqlite, a statement that changes no rows, such as `CREATE TABLE`, now reports the count of the last `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` rather than `-1` (apache/arrow-adbc#4820). A `dbExecute()` that violates a constraint now fails with the constraint's message and leaves the connection closable, where on `main` it fails with `INTERNAL: (unknown error)` and `dbDisconnect()` cannot close the connection afterwards (apache/arrow-adbc#4827). And `dbColumnInfo()` on a `dbSendStatement()` result now always fails, where it used to work once the statement had run and returned columns, as an `INSERT ... RETURNING` sent with `immediate = TRUE` does.

Fixes #92

title: Print a connection whose driver does not implement `GetInfo`
description:
## Summary

- Printing a connection whose driver does not implement `GetInfo` failed right after the `<AdbiConnection>` header with the driver's `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` status. The monkey driver that `adbi()` uses by default is one, and from source so is any driver built on the ADBC driver framework that leaves `GetInfoImpl()` at its default.
- The print method now catches `adbc_status_not_implemented` around that lookup, as `db_vendor_name()` already does, and prints the header alone in that case. Any other error still propagates.
- An open SQLite connection prints exactly as on `main`, and so does a closed one (adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-1).
- The new test prints a monkey connection and expects the header alone. It fails on `main` with the `NOT_IMPLEMENTED: GetInfo` error from the issue.

Fixes #104

title: Request only the labelled info codes when printing a connection
description:
## Summary

- Printing a connection ended in an `NA: NA` line with SQLite, PostgreSQL and DuckDB. The print method fetched every info code the driver reports, and all three also report code 103, the driver's ADBC API version, which it has no label for and whose `int64` value it does not read.
- The method now requests only the six codes it has labels for, so code 103 stays out, as does any code a driver adds later.
- With all three drivers the other five lines print exactly as before (adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1, DuckDB 1.5.5). From source, the Go driver base behind FlightSQL registers all six codes by default, so it too returns a value for each.
- The new test checks that every line after the header carries one of the six labels, and fails on `main` at the `NA: NA` line.

Fixes #101

title: Require a data frame in `dbAppendTable()` and warn on factors
description:
## Summary

- The `dbAppendTable()` method now fails when `value` is not a data frame, as the DBI specification requires, and leaves the table unchanged. It used to hand any list to `sqlAppendTable()`, which appended it. The check is the one in DBI's default method, worded like adbi's other argument errors.
- Factor columns are still appended as character, now with the warning the specification asks for. The factor conversion that `dbBind()` already did moves into a helper both methods call, without changing the warning `dbBind()` gives. Both checks run before the `INSERT` is built, so they carry over if #17 moves the method to ADBC ingest.
- DBItest's `append_table_invalid_value` and `append_roundtrip_factor` still skip because of #92, so new tests in `test-append-table.R` cover both cases; they fail on `main`. With the test helper's `rows_affected_callback` left out, `append_roundtrip_factor` passes. The `append_table_invalid_value` test now gets its error and an empty table, but its final comparison still fails: adbcsqlite reports every column of an empty result as int64, so the empty `DOUBLE` column reads back as integer. That is the same cause that fails the skipped `read_table_empty`.
- None of the CRAN reverse dependencies (db2pq, dbplyr, fabricQueryR) calls `dbAppendTable()` on an adbi connection. The dbplyr write paths go through `dbWriteTable()`, and DBI's default `dbAppendTableArrow()` converts factors itself before it calls `dbAppendTable()`, so it stays silent.

Fixes #95

title: Release the streams that metadata lookups read
description:
## Summary

- Reads the streams behind `dbExistsTable()`, `dbListTables()`, `dbListFields()`, `dbGetInfo()` and `show()` through `convert_stream()`, which releases each stream once it is converted. The internal `get_schema_objects()` and the `dbGetInfo()` and `show()` methods left them to the garbage collector, and until it ran, a `dbDisconnect()` released neither the connection nor the database, yet returned `TRUE` while the connection kept answering queries. These are the three sites in #97 that #99 left open when it added the helper for `connection_info_string()`.
- Adds one test per site that disconnects after the call and expects `dbIsValid()` to return `FALSE`: one for the three table lookups, which share `get_schema_objects()`, one for `dbGetInfo()` and one for `show()`. Each fails when only its own site is reverted.

Fixes #97

title: Qualify the name with the temporary schema in `dbRemoveTable()`
description:
## Summary

- Qualifies the name in `dbRemoveTable(temporary = TRUE)` with the schema of temporary tables on SQLite (`temp`), PostgreSQL (`pg_temp`) and DuckDB (`temp.main`), which all reject the `DROP TEMPORARY TABLE` that adbi has sent so far. RSQLite and RPostgres do the same, as do the ADBC drivers when they ingest into a temporary table ([SQLite](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/sqlite/sqlite.cc#L890-L892), [PostgreSQL](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/postgresql/statement.cc#L397-L399)). On DuckDB the shorter `temp` is ambiguous once a schema of that name exists. Deleting the keyword alone would drop a permanent table of the same name whenever no temporary one exists, and the new tests fail on that variant.
- Keeps `DROP TEMPORARY TABLE` for every other database. The keyword is MySQL syntax, and where it is accepted it drops only a temporary table, as in MySQL ([docs](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/drop-table.html)) and ClickHouse ([source](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/88e7eda66997e541fb50d7817d067ce8c4c38238/src/Interpreters/InterpreterDropQuery.cpp#L162-L174)); elsewhere it fails without dropping anything. Nothing changes for databases outside the three, and none of adbi's CRAN reverse dependencies (db2pq, dbplyr, fabricQueryR) pass `temporary` to `dbRemoveTable()`.
- Picks the schema through `db_vendor_name()`, which `dbDataType()` already uses for blobs: by driver class for adbcsqlite and adbcpostgresql, and otherwise by the vendor name from `adbc_connection_get_info()`, which DuckDB's driver reports as `duckdb`. That call's stream was never released, so a `dbDisconnect()` after the lookup left the connection open. The helper that reads it, `connection_info_string()`, now releases it through the `convert_stream()` proposed in #97, which covers one of the four sites listed there.
- Adds tests on SQLite that remove a temporary table next to a permanent one of the same name, a missing temporary table with and without `fail_if_missing`, and a table for a vendor adbi does not know, plus one that disconnects after the lookup through a Driver Manager manifest. The PostgreSQL and DuckDB schemas are unit-tested, since CI runs neither. DBItest's `remove_table_temporary_arg` still ends in the helper's `rows_affected_callback` skip before the call (#92). Without the callback it passes on SQLite, where `main` fails at the `DROP TEMPORARY TABLE`.
- Checked by hand against PostgreSQL 17.11 through adbcpostgresql 0.24.0.1, and against DuckDB 1.5.6 loaded from its C library through a Driver Manager manifest: only the temporary table is dropped, a second call errors, and `fail_if_missing = FALSE` succeeds even before the session has a temporary schema. On PostgreSQL, DBItest's `remove_table_temporary_arg` fails before the call, in a `dbCreateTable()` that asks for an ANSI `DOUBLE` column, which PostgreSQL lacks (#15).

Fixes #91

title: State the goals and non-goals
description:
## Summary

- Adds a "Goals and non-goals" section to the README, between the introduction and the installation instructions.
- The goals describe what adbi provides: DBI access to ADBC drivers in every form `adbi()` accepts, including the Driver Manager names and manifest paths from #60, DBI's Arrow extension, and conformance to the DBI specification as DBItest checks it.
- The non-goals mark out what belongs to other packages: implementing ADBC, shipping drivers, and defining the database interface.
- Reworked from the first version, which predated #60 and the one-sentence-per-line convention. A fourth non-goal is dropped, because two of its three examples were adbi's own behaviour. Its third example, temporary tables, led to #83.

title: Bind POSIXlt parameters as the equivalent POSIXct
description:
## Summary

- A POSIXlt parameter reached the driver as a struct column: the `I()` wrapping in `dbBind()` keeps it a POSIXlt in the data frame that gets bound, and nanoarrow represents POSIXlt as a struct of its components. Both adbcsqlite and adbcpostgresql reject that column, and CRAN's 0.1.3 fails the same way, with and without arrow.
- POSIXlt parameters are now converted to POSIXct next to the existing factor conversion, which covers list and data frame parameters alike and keeps time zone and `NA`. Parameters without a POSIXlt element come out of the new step identical to what went in, so the three reverse dependencies (db2pq, dbplyr, fabricQueryR) can only see a change where they previously got an error.
- DBItest's `bind_timestamp_lt` skips for the SQLite context, which sets `timestamp_typed = FALSE`, so the new test binds POSIXlt, as a list and as a data frame column, and compares against binding the POSIXct. It fails on `main` with the struct error.
- Against postgres, POSIXlt values now round-trip through a `timestamptz` column as the same instants as their POSIXct, under both a UTC and a Europe/Zurich session.

Fixes #89

title: Overwrite with ADBC's `replace` ingest mode in `dbWriteTable()`
description:
## Summary

- Overwrites through ADBC's `replace` ingest mode in `dbWriteTable()`. The `overwrite` branch used to drop the table with `dbRemoveTable()` and left `mode` unset, so the `paste0()` building the ingest option found `base::mode()` and errored after the drop.
- Fixes overwriting with `temporary = TRUE` along the way, which failed at the `DROP TEMPORARY TABLE` that `dbRemoveTable()` sends (#91). On SQLite and PostgreSQL alike, `replace` drops only the temporary table and leaves a permanent one of the same name alone. The `dbRemoveTable(temporary = TRUE)` part of #91 remains.
- Raises the adbcsqlite floor in Suggests to 0.11.0.1, its first CRAN release with `replace` support (apache/arrow-adbc#1355, the issue behind the removed TODO). The SQLite, PostgreSQL and Flight SQL drivers in arrow-adbc all handle the mode; with a driver that does not, overwriting errors, as it has in every adbi release since 0.1.0.
- Adds tests that overwrite an existing, a missing and a temporary table and read the result back, on a connection without the DBItest helper's `rows_affected_callback`. That callback turned the `-1` row count of the `DROP TABLE` into a skip, so DBItest's `overwrite_table` and `overwrite_table_missing` never reached the failing line. With `replace` they now run their checks, and still end in the callback's skip afterwards.
- Leaves the DBItest skip list as it is. Its `begin_write_commit` entry, listed under poorly understood causes, comes down to #72 and #92: without the callback both of its stages fail on `main` and pass here, but with it the first stage skips at its own `INSERT` and the second then fails, so the entry can go when #92 removes the callback.

Fixes #72

title: Raise `dbitest_version` in the DBItest helper to 1.8.3
description:
## Summary

- Raises `dbitest_version` in the DBItest helper from 1.8.0 to 1.8.3, which `DESCRIPTION` already requires, and drops the FIXME. Of the 47 tests DBItest added after 1.8.0, 36 now run: 8 pass, and 28 run until the `rows_affected` skip from #92 ends them. Four more skip on other tweaks.
- Adds three Arrow tests to the skip list. The Arrow versions of `read_table_empty` and `create_table_visible_in_other_connection` fail with the same message as those tests, which are skipped for apache/arrow-adbc#1400 and apache/arrow-adbc#1591: an empty table's character columns read back as numeric. In `arrow_write_table_arrow_visible_in_other_connection`, the `rows_affected` skip ends the first stage after DBI's default `dbWriteTableArrow()` has created the table but before it inserts any rows, so the later stages read an empty table. With the skip turned off, all three stages pass.

Fixes #93

title: Make parameter metadata optional when binding
description:
Closes #4 and supersedes #30 

Using `adbi` & `DBI::dbGetQuery` with `adbcsnowflake` currently errors unless the `immediate = TRUE` flag is set, as the `adbcsnowflake` driver does support returning parameter metadata/schemas.

This PR updates the handling for binding and schema-validation to skip validation when the driver does not support parameter metadata, allowing the query (with or without binding) to execute. Schema validation is still applied as normal if the driver can return that information.

This does mean that parameter errors would occur later (at binding/execution time) for drivers that don't return this info, but it allows the query to run without needing the `immediate = TRUE` argument

title: Re-enable DBItest's temporary-table tests
description:
## Summary

- Drops the `temporary_tables = FALSE` tweak from the DBItest context. It worked around apache/arrow-adbc#1141, which was closed in March 2024, and without it every temporary-table check that runs against adbcsqlite passes.
- Three of the re-enabled tests still stop before some or all of their temporary-table checks, at the helper's `rows_affected_callback` skip: `create_table_temporary_1` and `remove_table_temporary_arg` at `dbCreateTable(temporary = TRUE)`, and `remove_table_temporary` at `dbRemoveTable()`. That skip is not specific to temporary tables; it is the same one that hides #72.

Fixes #83

title: Lint without installing adbi in the smoke job
description:
## Summary

- Drops `local::.` from the smoke job's `extra-packages`, so the lint runs without an installed adbi and passes only if `.lintr.R` loads the checkout, as it has since #85.
- Nothing else in the job used the install: `roxygen2::roxygenise()` loads the package with pkgload, since `DESCRIPTION` sets no roxygen `load` option, and `check-r-package` installs the package it checks. The Website job keeps its own `local::.` for pkgdown.

Fixes #87

title: Bind plain R values without the arrow package
description:
## Summary

- Binding a plain R value with `dbBind()`, or through `params` in `dbGetQuery()`, `dbExecute()` and the like, failed whenever arrow was not installed. Each parameter is wrapped in `I()` so that `as.data.frame()` keeps list columns whole, and nanoarrow has no `as_nanoarrow_array()` method for `AsIs`, so it hands base vectors to arrow. Classed values such as Date, POSIXct and blob have methods of their own, which is why they bound fine.
- The `AsIs` class is now dropped again once the data frame is built. Across 22 inputs (each base type, `NA`s, multiple rows, named placeholders, raw lists, `dbExecute()` with `params`), the fix without arrow returns exactly what the unfixed code returns with arrow, and with arrow installed it changes nothing.
- Whenever arrow was missing, the DBItest runner skipped every test that binds plain values, so CI never saw this: the R 4.1 job installs no arrow. That skip list is now down to `roundtrip_raw`, whose `I()` list column reaches `dbWriteTable()` straight from the test. The other `arrow_*` tests pass without arrow too, as they only need nanoarrow. Against the unfixed `dbBind()`, the narrowed list fails 33 DBItest tests without arrow.

Fixes #82

title: Resolve lint names against the checkout, with testthat attached
description:
## Summary

- Loads the checkout with `pkgload::load_all()` at the top of `.lintr.R`, as the issue proposes, so that `object_usage_linter` resolves names against this checkout instead of an installed copy, and finds testthat attached as it is in a test run.
- Looks the path up before calling `load_all()`, rather than in its argument as the proposed line does. There the lookup would run only when the argument is forced, a dozen frames down in pkgload and rprojroot, and `dynGet("file")` would search each of those frames before the one of `sys.source()`. It reaches the right one today only because none of them binds a `file`.
- With adbi uninstalled, the 210 `object_usage_linter` lints on `main` are gone, whether `lintr::lint_package()` runs from the package root, from outside it, or from inside another package. Linting the head of #69 with `main`'s adbi installed, so are the three false positives the issue names: `get_parameter_schema()`, `skip_if_not_installed()` and `local_mocked_bindings()`.

Fixes #84

title: docs: Show a real result after `dbFetchArrow()` in the README
description:
The arrow-extension section of the README had a line that did not work sitting three lines above an identical-looking line that did.

`dbFetchArrow()` returns a `nanoarrow_array_stream`. A stream has no `length` element, so `ret$length` printed `#> NULL` in the rendered README. The chunked loop right below then writes `message("fetched ", ret$length, " rows")` and correctly prints `fetched 8 rows` — because there `ret` comes from `dbFetchArrowChunk()`, which hands back an array, where `$length` is real. Nothing on the page told a reader why the same expression worked in one place and not the other.

The stream is now materialised with `as.data.frame()`, which prints the ten rows the bound query returns. That also sharpens the contrast the section is already making: `dbGetQueryArrow()` a few lines above prints the stream object itself, `dbFetchArrow()` shows you how to turn one into a data frame, and `dbFetchArrowChunk()` below yields arrays whose `$length` is meaningful.

Re-rendered with `cynkratemplate::render_readme()`. Two consecutive renders produce a byte-identical `README.md`, so nothing machine- or time-dependent leaked into the output. This repository has no `index.md`; only `README.Rmd` and `README.md` change.

title: ci: Document with a patched roxygen2 that keeps the sentence gap
description:
Split out of #64 so it can be decided on its own.

## The problem

commonmark discards the whitespace a line break stands for. roxygen2 turns every softbreak into a bare newline, so the `.Rd` carries a line break with nothing after it and `Rd2txt()` renders it as a single space. Prose written one sentence per line therefore comes out single-spaced, while the same words wrapped to a fixed width with two spaces after the period keep the gap.

That makes the two styles mutually exclusive: splitting a sentence pair separated by two spaces silently drops one of them. That is what forced the very long single roxygen lines this package used to carry, because joining was the only way to keep the gap.

Only the text renderer is affected. `Rd2HTML()` and `Rd2latex()` differ by whitespace that HTML and TeX collapse — and LaTeX applies its own sentence spacing regardless. But text is what `?topic` shows, so it is the version most people read.

## The change

A new composite action, `.github/workflows/roxygen2-fork`, installs roxygen2 from upstream with the `R/` part of `krlmlr/roxygen2@f-sentence-spacing` applied on top, and `R-CMD-check.yaml` runs it immediately before the Roxygenize step.

It shallow-clones upstream, fetches the branch, computes the diff against their merge base restricted to `R/`, and applies it with `git apply --3way`. Restricting to `R/` means an unrelated upstream change to a test fixture cannot fail the documentation step. It aborts if the patch is empty or does not apply, rather than silently installing an unpatched build, and afterwards asserts that what it installed really carries the patch.

`Config/roxygen2/version` becomes `8.1.0.9100`. The `.9100` suffix distinguishes a patched build from upstream's own `.9000` development builds; if upstream moves, the `x.y.z` part follows it and the suffix stays. `DESCRIPTION` is DCF and cannot carry a comment line — `read.dcf()` rejects one as malformed — so the explanation lives in a `Config/cynkra/roxygen2` field.

## Why it is a separate pull request

Taking it changes rendered help across the package; leaving it means the reformatting below renders exactly as the package renders today, with one space between sentences. Neither half needs the other to be correct, so they should be able to be decided separately.

`man/` is not committed here, and it is not committed by the reformatting below either — every branch in this chain leaves `man/` byte-identical to `main`. CI regenerates it, so merging is what produces the updated `.Rd` files, and the diffs stay reviewable.

## Upstream

The roxygen2 side is `krlmlr/roxygen2#8`, on the fork, not yet filed with r-lib. It is deliberately narrow: mid-sentence breaks are untouched, links are unaffected, and two guards keep it from firing wrongly — an abbreviation list so a line ending in `e.g.` or `et al.` does not gain a mid-sentence gap, and a fix for a determinism bug where a line starting with `\doi{}` or `\code{}` gained or lost its gap at random, because the test was reading roxygen2's own random placeholder for protected Rd tags.

title: Start every sentence on its own line
description:
## Summary

- Starts every sentence of the roxygen documentation under `R/` and of `README.Rmd` on its own line, while lines within a sentence stay filled to 80 columns. Editing a sentence then reflows only that sentence rather than the rest of its paragraph, so documentation diffs stay small.
- Leaves paragraphs that already followed this as they were. No wording changes.
- Commits the regenerated `man/`, since `rcc` checks that the documentation is up to date. The rendered help is unchanged: `tools::Rd2txt()` gives identical text for every topic.
- Enforces the rule for the roxygen documentation with two custom linters in a new `.lintr.R`, which replaces `.lintr`. One flags a sentence that starts in the middle of a line, the other a sentence that starts with a lowercase word. They find the prose with the parsers that render it, roxygen2 for blocks and tags and commonmark for the markdown, so only the end of a sentence is detected heuristically. A genuine exception is silenced by wrapping the roxygen block in `# nolint start` and `# nolint end` comments, because a trailing `# nolint` on a `#'` line ends up in the help. The README is not covered, since lintr only checks the R chunks of an R Markdown file.
- Reworked from the first version, which also broke sentences at clause boundaries.

title: Drop the branch from the coverage badge, use one-word alt texts
description:
## Summary

- Drops the branch from the coverage badge, in the image and in the link, so both follow the default branch. A badge pinned to a branch keeps reporting that branch, and goes stale silently when the branch is renamed.
- Both URLs follow the snippet Codecov suggests for this repository, without its `token` parameter, which only private repositories need, and with the link pointing straight at `app.codecov.io`, where the snippet's address redirects.
- Gives the three badges one-word, lowercase alt texts: rcc, coverage and cran.
- Rebased onto `main` after #62 merged, keeping only the badge commit from the original stack.

title: Keep README.Rmd line breaks in README.md
description:
## Summary

- Renders the README with `github_document`, pandoc's `--wrap=preserve` and the `smart` extension turned off, so `README.md` keeps the line breaks, quotes and dashes of `README.Rmd` instead of being reflowed to 72 columns and typeset. Diffs of the rendered file then follow the source line for line.
- Reworked from the first version, which switched the output format to `cynkratemplate::readme_document`. In this repository that format writes no `index.md`, so what it contributed here were these two pandoc settings, which `github_document` takes directly without a dependency on cynkratemplate.
- Rebased onto `main` and re-rendered. The `README.md` diff is line wrapping only.

title: feat: support ADBC driver specs in `adbi()`
description:
Derived from #56

Fix #48

## Known ambiguity

Keeping implicit R-package lookup for bare strings creates unavoidable conflicts with ADBC driver names.

For example, with the duckdb R package installed, `adbi("duckdb")` resolves to `duckdb::duckdb()` instead of the ADBC `"duckdb"` driver and therefore fails, even if the DuckDB ADBC driver is installed.

This is why implicit package lookup through `driver` should be treated strictly as temporary compatibility behavior and removed after the deprecation period. `pkg =` provides the explicit replacement.

title: Move main to the next patch, 0.1.4, for development
description:
## Summary

- Moves `main` to 0.1.4, the number the next patch release would ship, under a "(development version)" NEWS heading, now that 0.1.3 is on CRAN. This follows the blockr packages rather than `usethis::use_dev_version()`: a `.9000` suffix pins no build that `RemoteSha` does not, and the NEWS heading is what marks the code as unreleased.
- Drops `development: mode: auto` from `_pkgdown.yaml`. That mode split the site on the `.9000` suffix, and at a plain 0.1.4 pkgdown resolves it to release mode, presenting unreleased `main` as the released version. Without it pkgdown uses its default mode and builds one site at the root, as the blockr sites do.
- Leaves out the DBItest development pin that the release dropped, so CI keeps testing against CRAN's DBItest.

The `dev/` copy on `gh-pages`, last built in December 2023 for 0.0.1.9000, is untouched by this. The deploy runs with `clean: false`, so it stays served at <https://adbi.r-dbi.org/dev/> until it is removed from that branch.

Fixes #76

title: Check reverse dependencies on release PRs, one job per dependent
description:
## Summary

- Adds a reverse dependency check to the `rcc` workflow for pull requests labelled `release`. It starts once smoke and the release gate have passed, next to the check matrix: a small job lists adbi's CRAN dependents, then one job per dependent installs it with its Suggests through `setup-r-dependencies` and checks it against adbi's CRAN release and then against the branch.
- A dependent's job fails only when a check does worse against the branch, as base R's `tools::check_packages_in_dir_changes()` reports it, and it writes both statuses and any changed checks to the run summary. None of these jobs is meant to be required.
- Moves the release gate from `release.yaml` into `rcc`, so that the check can wait on the gate and on smoke without a second workflow. The `rcc` workflow now also starts on `labeled`, so applying the label starts the release jobs, and any label change reruns it.
- Covers the dependents that only suggest adbi, which on CRAN are all three: db2pq, dbplyr and fabricQueryR. Each goes to `setup-r-dependencies` as a plain ref, since pak does not install the Suggests of an `any::` one, and without them dbplyr's adbi tests would skip. While adbi is not on CRAN, the listing job stops with a message saying so (see #78).
- Nothing on this pull request can run these jobs, so they were run locally, in a fresh `ubuntu:24.04` per dependent with R from rig, the install done by the same pak calls `setup-r-dependencies` makes, and the archived 0.1.2 standing in for CRAN's release. All three checked OK against both versions; on one core each, the installs took 139 to 282 s and each dependent's two checks 114 to 695 s.

Fixes #78

title: Prepare the 0.1.3 release for CRAN
description:
## Summary

- Bumps the version to 0.1.3, the first number above the archived 0.1.2, and titles the NEWS section with it. The section gains the unbound-statement fix from #32, which CRAN's 0.1.2 predates, and a PR link on each entry, and the 0.1.2 heading gets its correct year.
- Drops `Remotes: r-dbi/DBItest` and raises the DBItest floor to its CRAN release, 1.8.3, since CRAN's incoming checks reject both. The suite passes against 1.8.3.
- Keeps `.git` and `CRAN-SUBMISSION` out of the package build. In a git worktree `.git` is a file, which `R CMD build` otherwise ships.
- Prepares the docs for the review a new submission gets: a `\value` section on the four class pages, a `cph` role for the maintainer, an `inst/WORDLIST` for the release gate's spell check, and a misspelt class name fixed in the `dbConnect()` docs.
- Rewrites `cran-comments.md` to answer the archival reported in #61, and records the reverse dependency check there.

This stays a draft until the tarball goes to CRAN, and merges only once CRAN has accepted it.

Fixes #76

title: Add a release workflow running blockr.ci's release gate
description:
## Summary

- Adds `.github/workflows/release.yaml`, named `release`, which calls blockr.ci's reusable `release-gate.yaml` on pull requests carrying the `release` label.
- On such a PR the mechanical CRAN checks run on every push and report in one comment the gate rewrites each time; spelling, URLs and the `--as-cran` notes advise without failing.
- Ordinary PRs show one skipped job, and nothing joins the required checks. A job skipped at the caller never creates the called workflow's contexts, so requiring one means moving that condition inside first.

Fixes #74

description: Derived from #56

title: Replace the CI with a self-contained rcc workflow
description:
## Summary

- Implements the plan in #70: one workflow, `rcc.yaml`, built from r-lib/actions, replaces everything in `.github/workflows` and every reference to cynkra/cynkratemplate. Its `rcc` job passes only if the smoke, check matrix, no-suggests, coverage and website jobs all passed, and is the check the ruleset requires.
- The R 4.1 entry ignores arrow (`arrow=?ignore-before-r=4.2.0`), which needs R ≥ 4.2; without that, pak cannot resolve the dependencies. The plan's macOS source-build line isn't needed: the zstd copies on mac.cran.dev were stale cache entries, and it now serves gzip builds of every package in the dependency tree.
- Beyond the plan, the `Config/autostyle` fields go, since only the deleted style action read them, and the R 4.1.0 requirement gets a NEWS entry (#59 and #60 add the same heading, so merging `main` into them conflicts in `NEWS.md`). Third-party actions (codecov, JamesIves) are pinned to a SHA, while `actions/*` and `r-lib/actions` use major tags, as in r-dbi/odbc.
- Regenerating with roxygen2 8.1.0 leaves every Rd file byte-identical, so only `Config/roxygen2/version` changes. The lint fixes reword comments that lintr parses as code, issue references such as `apache/arrow-adbc#1141` among them, and rewrite one condition without the nested negation.
- Until this merges, the `rcc-status` workflow on `main` still posts an `rcc` commit status on this PR beside the new `rcc` check run; it mirrors the run's conclusion.

Fixes #70

title: Align handling of dbGetQuery without parameters to odbc::odbc()
description:
Using `adbi` with the `adbcsnowflake` snowflake driver currently fails to execute any queries unless the `immediate = TRUE` argument is set. 

The `odbc` package automatically sets the `immediate` argument if the [`params` argument is null](https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/bf7cd404b5417b925dbec1026ac559d1ee09d88d/R/dbi-connection.R#L237), which also solves the error here
